RAM pressure from a 63.7 GB memmap write beside a ~27 GB trainer is the suspicion and it is UNPROVEN. I checked VRAM headroom carefully before parallelising and never checked system RAM at all.

3. WHOLE_STACK died with 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote' at line 21. THIS ONE I CAUSED. bash reads a script incrementally by byte offset as it executes; a sweep that rewrote every arm's trailing marker truncated whole_stack.sh under the running shell, which resumed at a stale offset and died. It took a two-hour arm with it, and I did it while fixing the marker defect from loss 1.

WHAT IS FIXED, each verified by breaking it:
  - run_train reads PIPESTATUS[0], so a crashed trainer cannot be reported by a contented grep.
  - The completion marker moved INSIDE run_train and fires on success only, where success also requires a 'best holdout' line to exist - a trainer can exit 0 having produced nothing quotable.
  - Verdicts tee into the arm's OWN log. They used to go only to stdout, so the resolution arm was gated on a marker in a file that could never contain it; that gate would have waited forever with the GPU idle and nothing reporting an error.
  - run_snapshot copies an arm to <name>.running.sh and runs the copy, so the repo stays editable while long work runs. ARM_LIB carries lib.sh's path into the snapshot.
  - wait_for_cache gates on the cache MASK, which build() writes only after the decode loop returns. The images .npy is allocated at build START, and a build killed by the OS leaves no log line to grep for.

COST: roughly 50 minutes of GPU on arm U, a 2200-study decode, and a two-hour arm - against an afternoon whose entire measured yield was sub-bar anyway.

THE RULE WORTH KEEPING: never edit a file that is currently executing, and when a fix lands in shared plumbing, check what is running under the old copy.

title: Experiment definitions lived in /tmp - every number in the ledger came from an unversioned script
description:
RAISED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-11, and correct. Twenty-two chain scripts under /tmp produced every measurement this project reports. They were unversioned, unreviewable, absent from any diff, and one reboot from gone - so 'how was this number produced' had no answer in the repo.

This is the same failure the no-notebooks rule exists to prevent: a one-off run must become a committed entrypoint. A shell script in /tmp is a REPL session that happens to be a file.

FIXED: experiments/ is now in git.
  - experiments/lib.sh      shared plumbing, sourced by every arm
  - experiments/after.sh    queue an arm behind another's completion marker
  - experiments/arms/*.sh   one file per hypothesis, each carrying its control number and its result
  - experiments/README.md   the ledger

Three defects were fixed by the move rather than merely copied:
  - The data root is resolved through core.paths instead of a hardcoded D:/data, so an arm is runnable
    on another machine. paths.yaml is gitignored and machine-specific; the old scripts spelled it out.
  - run_train TEES full output to <processed>/experiments/<arm>.full.log before grepping. The old
    scripts piped straight into grep, so any traceback whose wording missed the filter vanished and a
    failed run looked merely empty.
  - wait_for exists so the completion-marker rule (knee-a9b) is encoded once rather than re-derived.

THE DIVISION: arms are CODE and live in git; logs and checkpoints are DATA and stay under processed/.

STILL TO DO: the arms that ran before the move (chains 1-15) exist only as their results in the ledger
and in interpretations/. Not worth reconstructing each as a file - but nothing new gets run from /tmp.
close_reason: Fixed in this commit: experiments/ is in git with lib.sh, after.sh, arms/ and a README ledger; all eight live arms syntax-checked and the path resolution verified against core.paths. New arms run from the repo, never /tmp.

title: Slot tie-break: two independent measurements say our data layer costs ~0.011-0.025 against the same weights
description:
TWO INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS OF THE SAME IMPERFECTION, both from the graft (knee-exd):
  - LOCAL: our pipeline reproduces the published members' own out-of-fold predictions to max|diff| 0.025, per-study correlation 0.99, under disjoint windows.
  - LEADERBOARD: the graft scored 0.888 public on the SAME 20 published members the public forks run, which sit near 0.899. Identical weights, so ~0.011 is what our data layer costs.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS: slot tie-break. SlotScheme.assign picks the densest stack and breaks a tie with max(), which keeps the FIRST maximal element in LIST order; their pandas sort_values keeps the first in FRAME order. A different series in a slot is a different image under the head.

STEP 1 MEASURED 2026-08-11 (kneemri/slot_ties.py, all 4,407 training studies, one DICOM header per series, no pixels):
  SAG_FLUID_FS     472  10.7%
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS   314   7.1%
  COR_FLUID_FS     115   2.6%
  AX_FLUID_FS      101   2.3%
  SAG_T1            42   1.0%
  COR_T1            39   0.9%
  AT LEAST ONE     894  20.3%

The hypothesis SURVIVES a test that could have killed it cheaply. One study in five has a slot where two series can both legitimately win, so the two pipelines have ample opportunity to disagree.

NOT CONFIRMED, and the gap between these two is the whole remaining question: a tie only matters when the tied series DIFFER in what they show. Two runs of the same sequence at the same slice count often differ only in acquisition time, and swapping them changes nothing. 20.3% is an upper bound on how often the routing can diverge, not an estimate of how often it does harm.

STEP 2, the measurement that would settle it: for the contested studies, decode BOTH tied candidates and compare - pixel distance, and then the model's own logits under each. If the logits barely move, the tie is harmless and the 0.011 lives somewhere else entirely (candidates: window policy, laterality, crop geometry, interpolation).

STEP 3 if step 2 says it matters: adopt frame order as the tie-break, which costs nothing and makes us agree with every published member by construction.

title: A training step sees 18 of ~180 slices: one window, never the volume
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-11, and it is the largest single change this project has measured.

THE CHANGE: read all 12 cached slices per slot per step instead of one random 3-slice window. A step goes from 18 images to 72 per study; with batch 12 that is 864 images through the encoder.

MEASURED, fold 0, small encoder, max pooling, rate 4e-5, against arm Q (identical recipe, WINDOWED read, best of 24 epochs) = 0.8310:
  whole-stack, 24 epochs   0.8413  peaked at epoch 6, then declined
  whole-stack, 12 epochs   0.8457  peaked at epoch 6 (still running at time of writing)
  +0.0147 on the control, and +0.0188 on the five members that produced our 0.888 leaderboard entry.

PRIOR ART SAYS THIS IS THE CANONICAL OPERATION, not an invention: MRNet (Stanford, PLOS Medicine 2018) combines per-slice features by an element-wise max over ALL slices of a series. Our three-slice window was the deviation. Found by looking outward BEFORE running the arm, which is how it should have been done for the knobs that preceded it.

WHY IT WORKS, in terms the earlier failures make sense under: the model was seeing 18 of ~180 acquired slices per step. The occlusion depth profile spans 0.7976 to 0.8332 across windows - larger than every method change measured here - so which window a step happened to draw was a bigger lever than any knob being tuned. Whole-stack removes the draw.

DOES NOT RESURRECT SLICE COUNT as previously tested: that arm was refuted under WINDOWED reading, where more slices at a fixed group of 3 means each group spans less tissue. Under whole-stack the mechanism is different and untested - see the new bead.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately not claimed: single fold, single seed. The fold ensemble now training is what turns this into a number worth quoting.

title: 9.9% of series match NO slot predicate, and three missing slots are 96% of it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 over all 4,407 studies (kneemri/slot_ties.py --lost, one DICOM header per series, no pixels).

THE PREMISE OF THIS ISSUE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. It claimed 17.4% of series 'never reach a slot'. That number conflated two very different losses:
  - STRUCTURAL: the series matches no slot predicate at all, so nothing can ever route it. This is 2,421 of 24,371 = 9.9%.
  - COMPETITIVE: the series matches a slot but loses to a denser stack, since one slot holds one series. That is the rest, and it is a different problem with a different fix (knee-evn).

THE CENSUS, and the reason it is actionable:
  Coronal|fluid|nofs   1139
  Axial|t1|nofs         621
  Axial|fluid|nofs      575
  Axial|t1|fs            57
  Sagittal|t1|fs         18
  Coronal|t1|fs          11
  83,297 slices in unrouted series - about 19 slices per study of imaging the model never sees.

NONE OF THESE ARE LOCALISERS. Coronal PD without fat suppression is a standard meniscus sequence; axial T1 reads patellar cartilage and the retinacula. These are diagnostic acquisitions the six-slot scheme simply cannot express.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND EXACT: the scheme covers three planes x two weighting axes only partly - there is no COR_FLUID_NOFS, no AX_T1 and no AX_FLUID_NOFS. Adding those three slots captures 2,335 of 2,421, or 96.4% of the structural loss. The remaining 86 are odd fat-suppressed T1s and can stay unrouted.

COSTS, stated honestly:
  - The cache gains a slot axis: 6 -> 9 slots is 35.8 GB -> 53.7 GB at 336 px and a full decode pass (~40 min).
  - A step costs 50% more encoder passes.
  - Every existing member has n_slot=6 and cannot load against a 9-slot head. The graft's 20 published members are 6-slot by construction, so the graft path must keep the 6-slot scheme - this forks the two, which is a real maintenance cost rather than a free win.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE WORTH HOLDING: a 2025 multi-plane study found single-plane sagittal beat three-plane fusion for ACL (0.976 vs 0.949), and our own anatomical-prior arm was neutral. More sequences is not automatically more signal, and this model already collapses its attention onto one slot (knee-1zk). The mechanism here is different - it adds sequences that are ABSENT rather than reweighting present ones - but the prior should temper the expectation.

title: comp/ is outside the enforced lint scope - 115 findings, and the submission path lives there
description:
PROGRESS 2026-08-11: the unambiguous half is done and committed. Fixed in comp/: unsorted imports (2), RUF010, SIM117 (urlopen + file are now one with-statement), E501, PLR2004 (0x2000 is now _PRINTABLE_CEILING with a docstring), and MissingToken -> MissingTokenError (N is in our select; the rename crosses publish.py). Verified by RUNNING verify_kit, publish's guard and survey's CLI, not just the linter. comp/ now passes ruff's enforced select except T201.

TWO POLICY CALLS REMAIN, each a decision rather than an edit:

1. T201 (84 prints). print is the interface of an operator CLI (verify_kit, build_kit) and the output mechanism of a Kaggle kernel, where the notebook log IS the console. kernel_run.py already uses logging, so conversion is possible. Options: convert everything, or widen lint_paths with a documented per-file-ignore for comp/kernels/** and the operator CLIs. The second is honest and cheap; the first is the house rule taken literally.

2. pyrefly missing-import x2. publish.py does 'from survey import ...' and 'from verify_kit import ...' - correct at runtime because the script's own directory is sys.path[0], unresolvable to a checker without a search-path entry. That entry lives in template-owned [tool.pyrefly] config, so it is a copier/upstream change rather than a local edit; adding them to ignore-missing-imports would be a suppression hiding a real structural fact - comp/ is a set of sibling SCRIPTS, not a package.

Only after those two can lint_paths gain 'comp'. comp/kit needs no exclusion: it is gitignored and both ruff and pyrefly already skip it.

title: Capacity is not the constraint - but 'capacity is spent' overstated it, and the rate prediction was refuted
description:
MEASURED, fold 0, 24 epochs, matched: large + every block trainable + ranking = 0.8304, against base + ranking = 0.8283. +0.0021 for 3.5x the parameters and 185s/epoch against ~50s. Inside noise, far inside the 1.5% bar.

THE MORE INTERESTING NUMBER IS THE CURVE: large peaks at EPOCH 10 and falls to 0.8211 by epoch 23, on a one-cycle schedule still decaying. small and base peak at 13-15 and hold. A model that peaks a third of the way in and then gives back 0.009 has more capacity than the supervision can constrain.

READING: the binding constraint has moved from capacity to SUPERVISION. 98.7% of our labels are read out of report text; 58 of 4,407 studies carry an image-read annotation.

PREDICTION LEDGER, recorded before the arms landed - kept open because two entries are still unresolved:
  - REFUTED 2026-08-11. 'The encoder-rate bracket should be neutral to NEGATIVE - a faster encoder is more capacity to fit noise.' Measured +0.0044 at 5x the rate (knee-3om). Wrong in DIRECTION. The magnitude is sub-bar, so this refutes the prediction without overturning the thesis - but the thesis is now weaker than when it was written, and the honest statement is that the encoder was frozen too hard, not that capacity is spent. A rate that HELPS is not what a supervision-limited model does.
  - OPEN: slice coverage should still pay - it adds EVIDENCE, not parameters. (Refuted for slice COUNT at fixed GROUP, -0.0016; the real test is whole-stack pooling, knee-hek / chain20.)
  - OPEN: the full-data fit should pay - 4,407 studies against 3,527 is more supervision (knee-7tq).
  - HELD: a large encoder, if used at all, wants a SHORTER schedule than 24 epochs.

DOES NOT resurrect label filtering - refuted on two matched seeds. Supervision-limited means more or better-READ labels, never fewer.

PRACTICAL: large is NOT the recipe to ship. base + ranking at 0.8283 costs a third of the wall-clock for a difference inside noise.

CLOSE THIS when whole-stack and the full-data fit have both reported - the thesis stands or falls on them, not on the capacity number that opened it.

title: The geometry laterality rule is unvalidated on the vendors that never write the tag
description: Header sweep over all 24371 series: the Laterality tag is absent on 50.7 percent of series and 50.0 percent of studies, and it is NOT missing at random - present on 84.3 percent of Siemens studies, 38.3 percent of Philips, and 0.0 percent of GE (868 studies), Toshiba (181) and Canon (45). So the geometry fallback is the SOLE laterality rule for about 24.8 percent of the corpus, and the 98.6 percent tag-vs-geometry agreement that validated it was necessarily measured only where the tag exists - Siemens and Philips. It has never been checked on GE or Toshiba. A left/right error there would suppress exactly the medial/lateral targets and is invisible to every check run so far. ALSO: this confounds the earlier refutation of the laterality hypothesis, whose first leg compared 'tag-resolved vs geometry-resolved' subgroups - those are near enough vendor subgroups. The second leg (rules agree 98.6 percent; asymmetry SMALLER on mirrored knees) is unaffected and remains the stronger argument. Cheap check: render a few GE and Toshiba coronal mid-slices after normalisation and confirm the medial compartment lands on the expected side.
close_reason: CHECKED AND THE RULE HOLDS. Population test with no eyeballing: after normalisation the mean coronal image of each vendor should resemble the tag-resolved reference and not its mirror. Correlation against the Siemens mean, straight vs mirrored - Philips 0.904/0.709, GE 0.925/0.730, Toshiba 0.913/0.721, with the floor set by Siemens against its own mirror at 0.780. A mirrored population would score at or below 0.780; every vendor scores 0.90+ upright. So the geometry rule agrees with the tag-resolved orientation on exactly the vendors that never write a tag. LIMIT: population-mean test, detects a systematic flip and not a sporadic one - a rule mirroring a random 5-10 percent would leave these numbers about where they are.

title: Test whether label CONTENT moves our score, before porting a 2000-line lexicon
description: REQUEUED at 24 epochs. The first attempt ran at 8 epochs and was killed mid-flight: 8 epochs is the regime just shown to be undertrained (24-epoch small scores 0.8205 vs 8-epoch 0.8081, +0.0124), so a label-content test there would have read as noise for the same reason eleven knobs did, and the whole point was a keep/kill on an expensive port. Design now: confident-only labels at seeds 2026 and 7, control full-labels at seeds 2026 (0.8205, already have) and 7, all 24 epochs, all scored against the FULL table so the struck-out arm earns no self-agreement credit. Two-vs-two against a 0.0062 floor is still thin but it is the right regime.
close_reason: Refuted with two matched seeds: striking the reader's own UNK calls (27% of pairs) costs -0.0073 (s2026) and -0.0056 (s7), same sign both times. Soft low-weight targets already extract the residual signal; filtering deletes real supervision. Written up in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11_what-actually-moved-the-number.md. Does NOT rule out a BETTER reader - that resolves UNKs rather than striking them - so knee-crl stays open at P2.

title: The slot head does not localise - it picks one axial slot for everything
description: RESOLVED to neutral. Corrected Baker's row (axial co-primary) scores 0.8073 vs baseline 0.8081 - indistinguishable at the measured 0.006 noise floor, where the first version scored 0.8005. One wrong row was worth 0.0068 of the 0.0076 regression. The structural finding STANDS and is the valuable part: the baseline head routes nearly every finding to AX_FLUID_FS (attention/anatomy correlation +0.127), so it is not localising evidence to the sequence that shows it. Forcing correct anatomy (+0.809 correlation) neither helps nor hurts, which says the slot choice is not where this model's accuracy comes from. Prior stays opt-in, default off: costs a parameter, buys nothing measurable.
close_reason: RESOLVED to neutral and recorded: forcing correct anatomy is 0.8073 vs 0.8081, indistinguishable. Prior stays opt-in, default off. The structural finding (attention routes nearly everything to AX_FLUID_FS) is preserved here and its live follow-up is knee-1zk, whose first step - quantifying the collapse as a score delta via attribution.slot_importance - is chain19.

title: Rebuild the ablation ledger on the recovered ruler
description: Noise floor is RULER-DEPENDENT and must be re-measured on report_labels_v2. On the old (lost) ruler two seeds spread 0.0012 (0.8233/0.8221, 30 epochs). On report_labels_v2 at 8 epochs, seed 2026 = 0.8081 and seed 7 = 0.8121, a spread of 0.0040 - 3x larger. If that holds with seed 13, per-slice max (+0.0018) is unambiguously noise and the anatomical prior (-0.0076) is ~2x noise rather than 6x. title: The measured ledger's ruler was unreproducible: the label table had no fetch step
description: Every ablation number (0.8092 baseline through 0.8221 floor) was scored against a report-derived label table that was NOT on disk anywhere - a drive-wide search for csv/parquet written since Aug 5 under D:/data returned nothing, and no copy existed in the repo or the kit. Recovered by re-downloading pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels (report_labels_v2.csv, the <target>/<target>__conf format Targets.load reads) and documented in comp/README.md as a required pre-training step. CONSEQUENCE: numbers produced before the recovery cannot be assumed comparable to numbers after it unless the same table was in use, so any new arm must be run as a MATCHED PAIR rather than compared to a ledger row.

title: Sample more slices at inference than at training (the .903 recipe's 12 -> 32)
description:
The scored .903 EfficientNet-B3 reference samples 12 slices per series while TRAINING and 32 at INFERENCE. We use 12 for both, and our cache is built at 12 — but the cache only constrains TRAINING. The kernel decodes the test split fresh, so reading 32 slices there costs nothing but decode time and needs no retraining and no new members.

WHY IT SHOULD WORK, and it is not the same lever as TTA: overlapping windows (already measured at +0.0025) re-read the SAME twelve cached slices in different groupings. Thirty-two slices covers more of the joint — a Baker's cyst sits at the posteromedial end of a sagittal stack, and the band sampler at twelve slices may simply never sample it. More windows re-slices what we have; more slices sees what we did not.

COST: decode scales linearly, so ~1 s per study becomes ~2.7 s. Against a kernel whose fixed cost is 542 s and a hidden set of order a thousand studies, that is roughly 45 minutes — affordable, and the existing degradation ladder (fewer windows, then fewer members) already exists if a run runs long.

MEASUREMENT, which is CPU-bound and therefore parallel to any training: decode the fold-0 holdout at 32 slices into its own cache, then score the SAME member at 12 and at 32 and compare. If it helps, it is free at submission time; if it does not, the twelve-slice band is already covering what matters and that is worth knowing too.
notes:
REFUTED, with a mechanism (2026-08-11). Scored on fold 0's holdout with member_fold0, matched on everything but the slice count:

  12 slices, disjoint (4 windows)    0.8281
  12 slices, overlap (10 windows)    0.8316   <- best
  32 slices, disjoint (10 windows)   0.8140
  32 slices, overlap (30 windows)    0.8137

Reading MORE slices is 0.018 WORSE, and more windows over those slices does not rescue it (0.8140 vs 0.8137).

WHY IT DOES NOT TRANSFER, which is the useful part: our encoder input is THREE CONSECUTIVE SLICES STACKED AS CHANNELS. The band (0.20-0.80 of the stack) is fixed, so at 12 slices a 3-slice group spans a certain physical thickness, and at 32 slices the same group spans roughly a third of that. The model is then shown groups whose through-plane extent it never saw in training — a different input distribution, not merely more of the same one.

The .903 recipe can raise its slice count precisely because its pooling is MAX OVER SLICE EMBEDDINGS: each slice is encoded independently, so more slices is more samples of a distribution that does not change. Ours couples slice spacing to the input through the channel stacking.

SO THE IDEA IS NOT DEAD, IT IS CONDITIONAL: it becomes available only if the group's physical thickness is held fixed while the slice count rises (sample 32 positions but keep the 3-slice group spacing at the 12-slice pitch), or if the aggregation changes to per-slice encoding. Both are real experiments; neither is the free win the recipe made it look like.

CONFIRMS SEPARATELY: overlap beats disjoint again at 12 slices (0.8316 vs 0.8281, +0.0035), consistent with the +0.0025 measured earlier on a different member.
close_reason: Refuted at 12->32 for OUR architecture: 0.8137 against 0.8316. Channel-stacked slice groups couple spacing to the input distribution; conditional revival paths recorded.

title: Intensity augmentation from cardiac-seg: the axis the public baseline does not touch
description:
IDEA SOURCE: ../cardiac-seg/core/data/dynamic/augment.py, where gamma / contrast / blur / noise are the transforms that measurably closed a CROSS-VENDOR generalisation gap on cardiac MRI.

OUR AUGMENTATION IS GEOMETRY-ONLY, and so is the public baseline's: rotation 8 deg, scale 0.08, shift 0.05, and a single global gain 0.10. There is no gamma, no contrast, no blur, no noise anywhere in either.

WHY THIS CORPUS SHOULD CARE MORE, NOT LESS: reports arrive in nine languages, so the studies come from many countries and therefore many scanners and protocols. That is the same nuisance variance cardiac-seg was fighting, in a harder form — and the hidden test set is where it bites, which is exactly the axis a holdout on the same corpus flatters.

TRANSFERRED WIDTHS (cardiac-seg's, adjusted): gamma (0.7, 1.5) at p=0.3, blur at p=0.2, contrast (0.85, 1.15), noise 0.02 — noise cut from their 0.08 because theirs acts on z-scored images and ours on [0, 1].

WHAT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and why the reason matters more than the setting:
- FLIPS. They flip both axes freely; a cardiac label is not side-defined. Here a horizontal flip undoes the laterality normalisation five of the twelve targets depend on.
- TRANSLATION. They measured it NEUTRAL and turned it off because a fully-convolutional U-Net is translation-equivariant. Our encoder is a ViT with position embeddings and is NOT equivariant, so the same measurement should not be inherited — it has to be re-run here.

PROVES IT: fold 0, matched against the 0.8201 augmented-geometric baseline. Intensity augmentation should help the HIDDEN test more than the holdout, so a flat holdout with a better LB is a possible and interesting outcome — which is an argument for spending a submission on it rather than judging it locally alone.
notes:
ARM C — INTENSITY AUGMENTATION IS +0.0019 ON THE HOLDOUT (2026-08-11), which is small and honestly near the resolution of a single matched fold.

  baseline  geometric augmentation only          0.8202
  C         + gamma / blur / contrast / noise    0.8221   (+0.0019)

CONTEXT THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST: turning augmentation on AT ALL was worth +0.011 (the never-called bug). Adding the intensity block on top of that is worth about a fifth as much on this measurement.

THE PRE-REGISTERED CAVEAT APPLIES, and it was written before the result: this transform targets CROSS-SCANNER nuisance variance, and the holdout is drawn from the SAME corpus as training — same scanners, same protocols. A same-corpus holdout is close to blind to the thing intensity augmentation is for. The hidden test is where it would pay, and a flat holdout with a better leaderboard was explicitly listed as a possible outcome.

So the result is compatible with both 'it does very little' and 'it does something the holdout cannot see', and this measurement cannot separate them. What it does establish: it does not HURT, which is not nothing — an augmentation that widens the input distribution could easily have cost accuracy on the narrow distribution being scored.

DECISION: keep it available but do NOT enable it by default on the strength of +0.0019. It is worth one submission slot later, when a submission is being spent anyway, precisely because the leaderboard measures the axis the holdout cannot.
FULL 2x2 COMPLETE (2026-08-11), fold 0, every arm scored on the pilkwang ruler:

                      pilkwang labels   v4_blend labels
  geometric aug            0.8202           0.8194
  + intensity aug          0.8221           0.8203

  intensity augmentation:  +0.0019 (old labels), +0.0009 (v4)   -> mean +0.0014
  better labels:           -0.0008 (geom),       -0.0018 (intensity) -> mean -0.0013

BOTH IMPORTED IDEAS ARE NULL on this measurement, and there is no interaction to rescue either.

THE PATTERN THIS SESSION, stated plainly because it is the most useful thing learned:

  fixing OUR OWN broken code   augmentation never called  +0.0110
                               missing LR schedule        +0.0061
                               TTA default left off       +0.0035
                                                          -------
                                                          +0.0206

  importing ideas from         intensity augmentation     +0.0014
  research and notebooks       better label table         -0.0013
                               32 inference slices        -0.018
                               label fusion               -0.0016 (vs best single)
                                                          -------
                                                          net negative

Fixing what we had was worth an order of magnitude more than adopting what others had, and every imported idea needed adapting or died on a mechanism specific to our architecture. That is not an argument against reading the field — the READING is what found the schedule, and the .903 notebook is what made labels checkable at all — but it is an argument against assuming a published gain transfers.

WHAT REMAINS LIVE: member count, the one difference we KNOW separates our 0.868 from the 0.888 graft. Two extra seeds on fold 0 are training now to price a member.
CORRECTION (2026-08-11): closed as 'null' on a single-fold matched pair, but seed variance on the same fold is +/-0.012 while these effects are +/-0.002. The correct verdict is NOT DETECTABLE at n=1, not null. Neither is worth re-running bigger — resolving 0.002 against 0.012 needs ~36 paired runs — but the record should not claim more than it measured. See knee-uxg.
close_reason: Null on holdout (+0.0014 mean). Kept behind --intensity-aug; the holdout cannot see the cross-scanner axis it targets, so it is worth one submission slot later, not a default.

title: train.py holds the best checkpoint in memory until the very end
description:
`train.py` keeps `best_state` as an in-memory dict and only calls `torch.save` after the final epoch. A process that dies at epoch 29 of 30 loses the entire fold — about fifteen minutes at the current recipe, and considerably more if the resolution or epoch count grows.

It nearly cost us already: the OneCycle off-by-one raised on the LAST STEP of the whole run, after every epoch had been logged and immediately before the save. The run was a total loss despite having produced its best epoch twenty minutes earlier.

It also makes the machine's own documented weakness expensive: suspend/resume on this box has a track record of killing GPU-adjacent state (the vpcivsp/WSL wedge), so an interrupted long run is a realistic event rather than a hypothetical.

FIX: write the checkpoint whenever `best` improves, to a temp path renamed into place so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated file. Optionally record the epoch and the RNG state so a fold can resume rather than restart.

DO NOT APPLY MID-RUN: the five-fold loop invokes `python -m kneemri.train` fresh per fold, so editing the module changes the recipe for folds that have not started yet. Apply after the current run completes.
close_reason: Trainer.save_partial writes each new best atomically (temp+rename) rather than holding it to the end

title: Loss normalisation: we divide by total weight, they divide by element count
description:
Ours:   (BCE * w).sum() / w.sum().clamp(min=1)
Theirs: (BCE * w).mean()

With most weights below 1, dividing by the weight sum makes our gradients roughly twice theirs for the same batch, and it makes the effective step size depend on how confidently the batch happened to be labelled. Theirs is a fixed scale.

Our normalisation was chosen deliberately ("a batch carrying little confidence should not take a full-sized step on almost no evidence") and that argument is still reasonable — but it interacts with the missing schedule, and an effectively doubled LR that never decays is a good way to plateau early.

Test it as a PAIR with the schedule, not alone: schedule-only, then schedule + their normalisation, on fold 0.
close_reason: REFUTED. Measured -0.0022 on top of the weight floor: dividing by element count instead of total weight is worse for us. Their normalisation is not transferable to our weighting. Recorded in the ledger.

title: Weight floor: a finding the report never mentions should pull weakly, not not at all
description:
We set the per-(study, target) loss weight to the confidence itself, so a target the report never mentions gets weight 0.0 and is DROPPED from the loss.

They use a floor:  W = 0.25 + 0.75 * conf  (annotated studies keep W = 3.0, which we already match).

The difference is not cosmetic. Silence in a radiology report is weak evidence of absence — a knee report lists what was checked and found intact, so an unmentioned finding is more often absent than present. Dropping it entirely throws that evidence away; a 0.25 floor keeps it at a quarter of the weight of an asserted one.

Pairs with knee-<LOSSNORM>: our loss divides by the total weight while theirs divides by the element count, so changing the weights also changes the effective step size. Change them together or neither, and measure both against fold 0.
notes:
RAISED IN PRIORITY by the augmentation find. Both the weight floor (0.25 + 0.75*conf vs our conf) and the loss normalisation (knee-sbr) are now the main un-tested differences from their recipe, since the schedule is measured (+0.0061) and epochs are refuted as a lever.

Test them against the AUGMENTED baseline, not the current one — the numbers below the augmentation fix are all from an unregularised model and are not the baseline anything should be compared to.
close_reason: Implemented as --weight-floor (W = 0.25 + 0.75*conf) and in every arm since. Measured +0.0019 - kept on mechanism (silence in a report is weak evidence of absence, not no evidence), recorded as noise by this project's bar. Its dependency knee-sbr is now closed as refuted.

title: Treat the rare findings as the expensive ones
description:
Every label costs the same 1/12 of the score. A label left at chance contributes 0.5 instead of ~M, forfeiting (M-0.5)/12 however well the other eleven do - at M=0.85 that is 0.029, larger than most modelling gains.

So rare findings deserve MORE attention than common ones, because a rare finding is where a model most easily ends up at chance. Track per-label AUC from the first run and treat the worst label as the work item, not the mean.

Prevalence drift is survivable (AUC is in expectation invariant to positive rate, and the competition does not guarantee matched prevalence across train/public/final); thresholds are not.

title: Encoder adaptation: unfreeze the last blocks, two learning rates
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11, and the inherited constants were both wrong in the same direction - too conservative.

RATE BRACKET (small + ranking, fold 0, seed 2026, control 0.8272):
  8e-6 inherited : 0.8272
  4e-5 (5x)      : 0.8316   +0.0044
  1.6e-4 (20x)   : ~0.739   collapsing - the encoder is destroyed

DEPTH BRACKET (at the inherited 8e-6, which is why it was uninformative):
  3 blocks : 0.8143   -0.0062
  6 blocks : 0.8205   control
  12 blocks: 0.8213   +0.0008

So the ORDER of the two questions was wrong: depth was bracketed first at a rate where no block moves, and read as 'depth is a ceiling at 6'. The rate is the binding constraint, and depth only becomes a real question once the encoder can move.

CAVEATS, both mine: +0.0044 is under the 1.5% bar (directional, not a result), and the 4e-5 arm moved rate AND depth together - the arm-J mistake again. Depth alone is +0.0008, so ~+0.0035 is the rate's share. Arm S (4e-5 at depth 6) isolates it.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW THE SCHEDULE: arm L was still improving at epoch 19 while the control peaked at 17 and declined. If a faster encoder needs longer, then the 8->24 epoch result - one of only two things this project counts as having paid - was measured at a rate where the encoder barely moves, and its magnitude is not transferable. Arm T runs 36 epochs at 4e-5.

STILL UNTESTED: whether the optimum sits between 8e-6 and 4e-5, or between 4e-5 and 1.6e-4. Not worth a sweep until a single-variable arm confirms the effect - sweeping a parameter before the effect is established is the stage-gate error this project has already paid for.
close_reason: RATE ISOLATED, 2026-08-11. Arm S (rate 4e-5, depth held at 6) = 0.8323 against control 0.8272 = +0.0051, single-variable. Arm L (same rate, depth 12) = 0.8316, so opening more blocks at the winning rate is -0.0007 - noise, and DEPTH IS NOT A LEVER at any rate tested. That closes the question this issue asked: it is the rate, not the depth, and the inherited 8e-6 was too conservative by about 5x. 1.6e-4 destroys the encoder (~0.739). Directional at +0.0051, under the 1.5% bar. Committed as experiments/arms/rate_isolate.sh. Remaining open threads live elsewhere: schedule duration on the winning config, and the composition with max pooling (experiments/arms/compose_small.sh).

title: Per-diagnosis query attention over slots, with a masked softmax
description:
Each of the twelve diagnoses gets its own query attending over the (up to six) slot embeddings, with absent slots masked OUT of the softmax so it renormalises over what the study actually contains.

WHY: mean-pooling the slots discards the reason the protocol has three planes - each finding is read on particular sequences, and a mean dilutes the one carrying the evidence with five that do not.

KEEP IT SMALL: the label is attached to the STUDY, so nothing in the supervision says which part carries the finding. Where the supervision is coarse, so is the head - a richer aggregator has no signal to learn from.
notes: IMPLEMENTED as kneemri/slot_head.py (SlotHead) during the Phase A port: per-diagnosis query, learned slot identity, masked softmax renormalising over present slots. Unit-tested including the property that masking a slot out equals never supplying it. Still to be trained by us - this is the replicated architecture, not our result.
close_reason: Shipped as kneemri/slot_head.py: per-diagnosis query, learned slot identity, masked softmax renormalising over present slots, unit-tested (masking a slot out == never supplying it). The note's remaining caveat ('still to be trained by us') is long overtaken - it is in every member we have trained, including the 0.8255 base@20 ladder point.

title: Report-derived labels: adopt the public tables, then measure whether we can beat them
description:
SPLIT IN TWO by evidence, 2026-08-11.

ADOPTED (done): pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels is the training table for every arm; the fetch step is committed after the ruler went missing once.

BEAT THEM (one branch now refuted): filtering the table by the reader's OWN confidence - striking the 27% of pairs it marks UNK - costs -0.0073 (s2026) and -0.0056 (s7), same sign in both matched seeds. So our supervision is not noise-limited in the way filtering would fix, and label CONTENT is not the free lever this issue assumed. See knee-5od.

STILL OPEN, and narrower: a reader that RESOLVES uncertain rows rather than striking them (the 0.899 notebook's multilingual negation scoping). That is the opposite operation and is untouched by the refutation. Gated behind knee-crl at P2 - the evidence now says the encoder, not the labels, is where our remaining gap lives.
notes:
THE DEFINING FACT, measured (probe v2, train.csv 4407 x 14): all 4407 studies carry a Report, and only 58 carry all twelve annotations.

58 / 4407 = 1.3%. The competition is therefore a weak-supervision problem first and an imaging problem second: the labels for 98.7% of the training corpus have to be read out of free text, in nine languages, or not exist at all. This is why every top notebook mounts the same public LLM label tables, and why improving those tables is the highest-leverage un-shared axis available.

Prevalence among the 58 annotated studies: Effusion 0.603, Synovitis 0.466, Medial Meniscus 0.448, ACL 0.414, Lateral Meniscus 0.397, PF OA 0.362, Contusion 0.328, Fracture 0.310, Medial OA 0.259, Baker's 0.207, Lateral OA 0.190, MCL 0.155.

Read that as counts, not rates: MCL has NINE positives, Lateral OA eleven, Baker's twelve. Any model-selection decision made on the annotation check is being made on single-digit positive counts - which is exactly the Hanley-McNeil argument for why the holdout, not the annotation check, must arbitrate.
FIRST TRAINED MEMBERS (2026-08-10) on the public LLM report labels (pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels, CC0): 5 folds x 16 epochs, holdout mean AUC 0.8092 / 0.8177 / 0.8108 / 0.8179 / 0.8252, mean 0.8162. Selected on a holdout split by REPORT-TEXT HASH so duplicate reports cannot straddle the divide.

The published members average 0.8398 on their own holdout, so we are ~0.024 under the frontier after one training run. That gap is now a MEASURED quantity, which is what makes it attackable: the labels are the shared input everyone mounts, so beating the public tables is the un-shared axis - and our number moving without the labels changing would say the gap is in the model instead.

Training cost: 27s per epoch on the 5090 over the 35.8 GB memory-mapped cache. Cheap enough that epochs and folds are not the constraint - what to train ON is.
PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE for the next submission (2026-08-11, written BEFORE the folds finished):

SUBMIT if the new five-fold holdout mean is >= 0.825. Otherwise do not spend a slot.

Reasoning: the old ensemble averaged 0.8162 with a fold-to-fold spread of about +/-0.008, so anything under ~0.825 is inside that spread and proves nothing. Fold 0 has already reproduced +0.011 on a MATCHED comparison (same fold, same seed, only the recipe differing), and overlap TTA adds a measured +0.0025 on top, so the threshold is what the two changes should deliver if they hold across folds rather than being fold-0 luck.

Written down in advance so 'notable' cannot be decided after seeing the number.
close_reason: ADOPTED half done (report_labels_v2 is the table for every arm, fetch step committed). BEAT-THEM half: one branch refuted (confidence filtering, -0.0073 / -0.0056 on two matched seeds), the surviving branch - a reader that RESOLVES uncertain rows via multilingual negation scoping - is knee-crl. Closing so it stops blocking knee-3om; the live work is knee-crl.

title: Decode-once pixel cache under a memory budget
description:
Decode slot images once into a uint8 in-memory cache; bytes = studies * slots * slices * P^2. Training draws one group of consecutive slices per step (doubles as augmentation along the stack); inference averages over groups.

WHY: a study is ~150 files and the pipeline is read-bound, not arithmetic-bound. Affordable once, not once per epoch.

CONSTRAINT: the cache grows with the SQUARE of resolution and only linearly with slices, so slice coverage is the cheap axis and resolution the expensive one. Budget a fraction of free memory (not all of it) and size TRAIN + TEST caches together, since both are resident at once - overshooting ends the run rather than slowing it.
close_reason: Shipped as kneemri/study_cache.py: decode-once uint8 memmap, images_336px_12sl.npy = 35.8 GB on disk, one contiguous slice per batch. The memory-budget constraint is honoured by memory-MAPPING rather than resident allocation, which is a better answer than the budget the issue asked for.

title: Physical-scale crop + resample (mm/pixel is the design variable)
description:
Crop to a constant physical extent L and resample to P pixels, so effective pitch = L/P mm/pixel.

MECHANISM: a feature of width d survives only if pitch <= d/2 (Nyquist on the resampling grid). A meniscal tear is 1-3mm, so 1mm needs <= 0.5 mm/px. At L=130mm: P=224 gives 0.580 (fails), P=336 gives 0.387 (clears). The crop must be SMALLER than the smallest field of view or it silently does nothing.

PROVES: measure the acquired FOV distribution (Rows * PixelSpacing) over our training series. The claim to check is median ~160mm, range 70-320, and that 130mm sits below the FOV of ~99.6% of series. Pick L from OUR measurement, not from the quoted one.
close_reason: Shipped at L=130mm, P=336 (0.387 mm/px, clears the 0.5 mm/px Nyquist bar for a 1mm tear). PROVES clause satisfied on our own copy: FOV median 160mm, 1st percentile 130mm, only 0.43% of series narrower than the crop - so it crops rather than pads. Pixel spacing median 0.3125mm; the 9.6% coarser than 0.5mm are interpolated past native resolution, which is the group where a 1mm tear was never resolvable anyway. Written up under 'Corpus facts, finally measured on our own copy'.

title: Laterality normalisation, including recovery when the tag is absent
description:
Five of twelve targets are side-defined (two menisci, medial/lateral OA, MCL). Normalise: flip the last axis for coronal/axial (medial-lateral is in-plane); REVERSE THE SLICE ORDER for sagittal (medial-lateral is the slice axis).

Laterality is Type 2C and reported absent on half the studies, by whole vendors. Recover from patient coordinates: image centre c = p + r*ds*Nc/2 + d*dr*Nr/2; +x points to the patient's left, so sign(c_x) gives the side. Use the CENTRE, not p (a corner half a FOV away can flip the sign near the midline). Leave a study unresolved inside a ~20mm dead band rather than guessing.

PROVES: on our data, measure the Laterality-tag absence rate and its per-vendor concentration; check the recovered side against the tag where both exist.
close_reason: Shipped as kneemri/laterality.py with the geometry fallback. PROVES clause satisfied twice: tag absent on 50.0% of studies and NOT at random (GE/Toshiba/Canon 0.0%, Philips 38.3%, Siemens 84.3%); where both rules exist they agree on 98.6% of 2135 studies. The gap that left - the geometry rule was validated ONLY where the tag also exists - was closed separately by the mean-image check on the vendors that never write it (GE 0.925 upright vs 0.730 mirrored, floor 0.780).

title: Three of the five OneCycle knobs are PyTorch defaults nobody chose
description:
AUDIT prompted by the owner asking what scheduler we use. It is OneCycleLR, whose anneal_strategy defaults to 'cos' - so the project already has cosine, inside one-cycle, and there is no separate cosine path.

OURS, with a measured reason: max_lr per parameter group ([head 1e-3, backbone 8e-6, now 4e-5]) and pct_start=0.15. The justification is real and recorded - at a CONSTANT rate our five folds peaked at epochs 13/13/10/12/11 and gained ~0 over their final five, so a run that improves to 60 epochs is training on a decaying rate rather than training longer.

PYTORCH DEFAULTS, never chosen by us:
  anneal_strategy='cos'
  div_factor=25        -> the run STARTS at max_lr/25
  final_div_factor=1e4 -> the run ENDS at max_lr/250,000, i.e. effectively zero for the last stretch

WHY THIS IS WORTH A LOOK GIVEN TODAY: the session's pattern is that every constant inherited rather than measured has turned out load-bearing once it got a flag - the encoder rate (5x helped), the unfreeze depth (uninterpretable at the inherited rate), the slice count, the group thickness. div_factor is the same shape of thing: with the rate finding suggesting the encoder was frozen too hard, a warmup that STARTS the backbone at 4e-5/25 = 1.6e-6 - below the inherited constant rate - deserves questioning.

NOT QUEUED, deliberately. The rate effect is not yet confirmed single-variable (arm S), and sweeping a schedule parameter before the effect it interacts with is established is exactly the stage-gate error this project has already paid for once.

ALSO NOTED, and it affects a running arm: because OneCycle is defined over total_steps, arm T (36 epochs at 4e-5) stretches the whole cycle rather than merely adding duration - warmup goes 3.6 -> 5.4 epochs and the decay slows to match. It tests schedule SHAPE and duration together. That is the right thing to ship, but it must not be read as 'more epochs helped'.

title: Decide the epoch-selection read policy: 3 windows, or document the mismatch
description:
AUDIT. The slice stack is read three different ways in one project:
  - TRAINING LOSS: one RANDOM 3-slice window per step (trainer.py:282), same start for every study in the batch.
  - EPOCH SELECTION: Trainer.predict reads the MIDDLE window only.
  - DEPLOYMENT (submission, ruler_check, attribution): 10 OVERLAPPING windows, averaged.

So the epoch kept as 'best' is chosen under a policy the shipped model never uses.

MEASURED, across seven checkpoints holding both numbers: overlap beats middle by a near-uniform +0.0156 (min +0.0127, max +0.0172). Ranking is essentially preserved - one swap, deep24_s2026 vs ep24_fold0, which sit 0.0008 apart and are tied in any case.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, one benign and one not:
  BENIGN: our comparisons are not distorted, so no recipe decision made this session is invalidated.
  NOT: every local number understates deployment by ~1.6%, which is LARGER than any single method change measured today (ranking +0.005, base +0.0085, 8->24 epochs +0.0068). TTA is the biggest single contributor we have, and it was already in the submission path rather than being a finding.

WHAT IS STILL UNTESTED: whether epoch SELECTION within a run would choose a different epoch under the deployment policy. That needs per-epoch states, which we do not keep. The near-uniform gain (spread 0.0045) suggests mostly not.

FIX OPTIONS: score epochs on 3 windows (first/middle/last) rather than 1 - a cheap approximation that removes most of the mismatch; or accept the mismatch and document it. Full 10-window scoring per epoch would add ~10x the eval cost to every epoch, which is not worth 0.0045 of ranking fidelity.

title: A queue gate fired on a file written at BUILD START, not completion
description:
chain13 waited on index_336px_20sl.json to decide the 20-slice cache was ready. build_cache writes that index at the START of the build (timestamp 11:47, while the log still read 3600/4407), so the gate was already satisfied and the arm would have begun the moment the GPU freed - training on a 59.7 GB array still mostly zeros.

It would NOT have crashed. It would have produced a plausible, wrong number for the slice-coverage question, which is the failure mode this project keeps meeting: the run completes and the result is quietly meaningless.

Caught before firing only because chain12 still had ~65 minutes left. Requeued on 'CACHE BUILD COMPLETE', which build_cache logs as its final line.

RULE, same family as knee-74x and knee-b02: a readiness gate must key on a marker the producer writes when it FINISHES. An output path proves the job started, never that it ended.
close_reason: chain13 re-gated on 'CACHE BUILD COMPLETE'; chain14 now asserts every checkpoint path exists before spending GPU. The rule (gate on a completion marker, never on an output path) is recorded here and applied.

title: The kit was stale AND had lost its wheels; both guards caught it
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-11. comp/kit had drifted from kneemri/: backbone.py, ema.py, targets.py, train.py, trainer.py all differed and objective.py was missing entirely. The wheels were gone too - build_kit rebuilds from scratch and drops them unless run WITH --wheels, which comp/README already warns about.

BOTH GUARDS WERE VERIFIED BY BREAKING THEM, not by reading them:
- publish.py refused with the exact file list, exit 1, BEFORE authentication (its docstring's claim, confirmed in both directions: after the rebuild it clears staleness and stops at the missing token instead).
- verify_kit.py, with a wheel removed, said 'missing wheel: jaxtyping (kernel will fail at import)' and exited 1; green again on restore.

So this needed no fix - the design is right and it worked. Recorded because the SYSTEM is what deserves the credit: the kit is gitignored (no duplicated source in git), it goes stale by construction on every kneemri/ change, and the gate sits at publish time where it is fail-safe. Auto-rebuilding on commit would HIDE the drift rather than catch it.

Kit rebuilt and verified; nothing published - that is the owner's call.

STANDING RULE: after any session that touches kneemri/, run 'uv run python comp/build_kit.py --wheels <dir>' then 'uv run python comp/verify_kit.py' before any submission.
close_reason: No fix needed - both guards were verified by breaking them and the standing rule already lives in comp/README.md:52-66, which is where it is read. Nothing left in the tracker.

description: The testing policy in CLAUDE.md specifies three layers; integration is now filled with the checkpoint-to-submission chain, e2e is still an empty directory. title: Queue scripts must use python -u and a real process-kill path
description: Two operational defects cost time this session. (1) Piping train stdout through grep buffers it, so a 45-minute arm showed NO epoch lines and progress could only be inferred from the .partial checkpoint mtime; python -u fixes it and is now used in the chain script. (2) pkill does not exist in this Git-bash environment - it fails with 'command not found' and the failure looks like success in a compound command, so an earlier 'kill the queue' silently did nothing. Use PowerShell Get-CimInstance Win32_Process + Stop-Process -Force, matching on CommandLine. Both are why a confounded arm ran for 7 minutes before being caught.

title: Non-English reports: weaker labels and a 0.016 score gap on 54% of the corpus
description: DEFLATED, do not build the parser on this evidence. The gap survives restricting to confident labels (0.0119 all vs 0.0117 at conf>=0.7), so it is not simply ruler noise. BUT scanner model predicts report language almost deterministically (MAGNETOM Avanto fit 0 percent english over 262 studies, Optima MR450w 100 percent), the between-manufacturer spread (0.8020-0.8256) is LARGER than the language gap and does not order by english share (best group is 50 percent english), and field strength shows nothing (1.5T 0.8159 vs 3.0T 0.8156). Language is confounded with site. Subgroups are small (111-223) so the manufacturer ranking is not itself established. A nine-language label parser targets the one reading the evidence does not isolate.

title: Two seed members on disk have an unrecoverable recipe
description: seed7_fold0.pt and seed13_fold0.pt were trained by an inline queue whose flags were not saved and whose script is gone. Checkpoints recorded image geometry but not one_cycle/weight_floor/intensity_aug, so neither can be matched to a seed-2026 counterpart and neither can serve as a noise floor on its own. train.py now writes an 'options' block (str-valued, since every loader uses weights_only=True and it refuses Paths). If a clean noise floor is needed, run three seeds under one explicit recipe rather than trusting these two.

title: Rebuild the kit whenever kneemri/ changes, not only when weights change
description:
A kernel run died on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kneemri.submission'`. The kernels had been refactored to import a newly extracted module, the MEMBERS dataset was pushed with the new weights, and the KIT — which is what actually carries our source into the kernel — was not.

`comp/verify_kit.py` exists precisely for this and takes a second to run. It was skipped because the change felt like it was 'only in the kernels', which is exactly backwards: the kernels are a bootstrap that imports the kit, so a change to either is a change to both.

CHEAP FIX AVAILABLE: make the push path refuse to run a kernel against a stale kit. `publish.py kernel` could call the same drift check `verify_kit.py` performs before pushing, so the ordering cannot be got wrong by remembering. Filed rather than done because the immediate cost was one kernel run and pushes are unlimited — but it will recur every time a module is extracted.
close_reason: publish.py now runs verify_kit's drift() in main, before auth, on every subcommand

title: cls_mean_focal pooling — implemented, unused by us AND by their shipped members
description:
`StudyModel._pool` already implements `cls_mean_focal`: class token, patch mean, plus the mean of the top eighth of each channel over the patch grid. Every published member uses plain `cls_mean`, so this is an untested axis for BOTH of us — an ablation, not a copy.

The rationale is quantitative: at 336 px the patch grid is 24x24 = 576 tokens, and a meniscal tear occupies a handful of them, so a plain mean dilutes the signal by roughly two orders of magnitude. That is the same argument the resolution choice was made on.

Costs one flag and a retrain (~5.5 min per member). Worth running against the settled recipe, not against the current one.

title: Scale to 20 members (5 folds x 4 seeds) — buys rank, teaches nothing
description:
The one difference we KNOW separates the two ensembles: theirs is 20 members (5 folds x 4 seeds), ours is 5. At ~12 epochs a member costs ~5.5 min, so 15 more is ~80 minutes, and members are nearly free at inference (20 members cost 575 s of kernel time against 5 members' 542 s — the fixed cost dominates).

Deliberately ranked BELOW the schedule and the diagnostic. It is the most predictable gain available and the least informative one: it would raise the leaderboard number while leaving every open question exactly where it is. Its real value is giving the other changes a stable ensemble to be measured against, so run it AFTER the recipe is settled, not before.
notes:
WHY THIS IS NOW THE PRIORITY, and how to measure it cheaply (2026-08-11).

The largest KNOWN difference between our 0.868 submission and the 0.888 graft is member count: 5 against 20. But the two also differ in per-member quality (0.8269 against their 0.8398), so the 0.020 leaderboard gap is a mixture of both and neither is attributable yet.

THE MEASUREMENT CANNOT BE TAKEN FROM WHAT WE HAVE. Our five members are five different FOLDS, so four of them trained on fold 0's holdout — ensembling them there would score a model on studies it was fitted on. Member count has to be varied with the fold held fixed, which means SEEDS.

QUEUED: two extra seeds for fold 0 (30 minutes), giving three members on one holdout. That yields the marginal-member curve — single member, then two, then three — and the shape of that curve says whether going to twenty is worth 2.5 hours of GPU or whether it saturates at four or five. Rank-averaging is the combiner, as the metric demands.

Ranked above further label work because arm A came back flat: the label lever is unproven on the model's own measurement, while the member lever is the one difference we KNOW separates our submission from the better-scoring one.
SEED VARIANCE IS +/-0.012, WHICH RETROSPECTIVELY WEAKENS MY OWN ABLATION CONCLUSIONS (2026-08-11).

Fold 0, identical recipe, identical data, only the seed differing:
  seed 2026   0.8202
  seed 7      0.8323     (+0.0121)

Every single-fold ablation I ran this session has an effect size FAR below that spread:
  intensity augmentation  +0.0019
  better labels           -0.0008
  both together           +0.0001

I reported those as 'null' and closed two issues on them. The honest statement is weaker: AT SEED 2026 the effects are small, and a single matched pair CANNOT RESOLVE an effect six times smaller than the run-to-run spread. 'Not detectable at n=1' is not the same as 'null', and I wrote the stronger claim.

WHY MATCHED SEEDS DID NOT SAVE IT, which is the subtle part: matching the seed fixes the initialisation and the data order, but every arm changes the random STREAM — augmentation draws differ, so the arms diverge stochastically much as different seeds would. Matched-seed is not paired in the way it looks.

WHAT SURVIVES: the five-fold result (+0.0107, every one of five folds improving) is a paired comparison across five independent splits, and five-for-five is not seed scatter. The bug fixes stand.

WHAT DOES NOT: the 2x2. To resolve a +0.002 effect against a +/-0.012 spread needs roughly (0.012/0.002)^2 ~ 36 paired runs, which at 15 minutes each is nine hours for one cell. That is not worth it for an effect that small — the correct conclusion is 'too small to matter at our current distance from the frontier', and the experiment should not be repeated bigger.

THE PROJECT'S OWN RULE SAID THIS: 'once a result works, multi-seed; never read signal into single-seed scatter'. I applied the first half and skipped the second.

SILVER LINING, and it is a real one: a +/-0.012 seed spread means ENSEMBLING SEEDS should pay well, because averaging independent runs of this variance is exactly what rank-averaging is for. That makes the member-count experiment more promising than it looked, not less.
VOID — THE MEASUREMENT WAS LEAKY, AND THE BUG WAS OURS (2026-08-11).

`train.py` built the fold split from the TRAINING seed: ReportFolds(folds, arguments.seed). So the extra seeds did not re-train the same setup on the same split — they trained on DIFFERENT splits. seed 7's fold-0 holdout shares 192 of 909 studies with seed 2026's.

CONSEQUENCES, all of them mine to retract:
1. 'Seed variance is +/-0.012' (0.8202 / 0.8323 / 0.8282) is unfounded — three numbers on three different holdouts of different difficulty, not three samples of one quantity.
2. The marginal-member curve (+0.0053 for the second member, +0.0018 for the third) is VOID: it scored seed 7 on seed 2026's holdout, 717 studies of which were seed 7's training data. That is what produced an implausible 0.8807 for a member that logged 0.8323 in its own run.
3. The correction I wrote to the interpretation document — downgrading the ablations against a +/-0.012 noise floor — rested on (1) and has itself been corrected.

THE BUG FAILED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION, which is why it was worth catching: leakage makes numbers BETTER, so nothing looks wrong until a value is implausible enough to question. 0.8807 was implausible only because a matched measurement of the same member existed at 0.8316.

FIXED: --split-seed is now separate from --seed and defaults to 2026, so the split is a property of the corpus rather than of the run. A test asserts that changing the model seed does not move the split.

STILL UNMEASURED, and to be redone with the fix: the run-to-run noise floor, and the marginal value of a member. Both need seeds that differ ONLY in initialisation.
close_reason: Curve measured on the recovered ruler, three seeds, one split: 1 member 0.8204 [0.8171-0.8233], 2 members +0.0018, 3 members +0.0007. Best SINGLE member (0.8233) beats the 3-member ensemble (0.8229). Ensembling buys ~0.002 for 3x inference. Caveat: these differ only by seed on one fold, so it is a LOWER bound - the submitted 5-fold ensemble also varies training data.

title: comp/SUBMISSIONS.md: method-tuple naming + coverage grid
description:
Mirror the biohub convention: kernels named for the method tuple from a closed vocabulary, one subdir per method, and a coverage grid recording what has been tried vs what has not. The slug says which method it is; a new version of one slug is that same method retrained.

WHY: without it, submissions become an unlabelled pile and the 5/day budget gets spent re-running things whose result is already known. It is also where a grafted score is recorded AS a graft.

title: Decide whether to target the Efficiency Prize
description: BLOCKER RESOLVED - the track is additive, build the cheap kernel. Joined the efficiency leaderboard to the public one on team name, 897 teams in common: 61.3 percent identical scores, 38.7 percent (347 teams) carry an efficiency score STRICTLY BELOW their public best (median 0.018 lower, never higher). The efficiency leader is public 0.939 / efficiency 0.934. So teams hold both a high-accuracy public entry and a separate cheaper efficiency entry; a cheap submission adds a candidate rather than displacing the accurate one. Combined with the flat member curve (best single member beat the 3-member ensemble) and teams at our 0.888 sitting at efficiency ranks 29-50, a one-member overlap-free kernel is close to free rank. Remaining work is the kernel itself: strongest(1) + Submission(overlap=False).

title: Combine members by rank, not by probability
description:
The score is the unweighted mean of twelve per-label ROC AUCs, invariant under any strictly increasing map, so calibration and thresholds are worth exactly nothing.

Averaging raw probabilities lets the most confident model dominate; averaging RANKS combines the only information the metric reads. Applies to member ensembling and to TTA pooling (logit-averaging is a geometric mean of odds, probability-averaging an arithmetic mean of risk - they order studies differently).
close_reason: Implemented and shipped: ensemble.py:110-116 ranks per label via argsort().argsort(), normalised, then means over members. Docstring at ensemble.py:7-8 carries the reason.

title: Members carry their preprocessing; verify by fingerprint before use
description:
A trained member is only reproducible together with the reading that produced it: resolution, crop, slice-order rule, laterality rule, slot-fill predicate, and the stand-in for a slice that will not decode. NONE of those change a single tensor shape.

So a member fitted under one reading and run under another loads cleanly, runs, and returns a submission computed from the wrong image. Ship the reading WITH the member, and have each member answer a seeded question whose expected answer travels with it; a mismatch stops the run rather than being averaged into a submission.

Group members by the pixels they need so one decode serves every member sharing it.
close_reason: Implemented and PROVEN: members carry their config, StudyModel.fingerprint answers a seeded question, and the graft-verify kernel reproduced 20/20 stored fingerprints at worst max|diff| 4.65e-06 against a 2e-3 tolerance. Members are grouped by pixel_group so one decode serves all sharing it. The submission path stops on a mismatch.

title: Backbone ablation: DINOv2 vs medical-pretrained
description:
Every public notebook mounts metaresearch/dinov2/PyTorch/small/1. Alternatives are already packaged as Kaggle datasets: RadImageNet ResNet-50, MedicalNet ResNet-50 (3D), BiomedCLIP.

The field defaulted to DINOv2 with no visible evidence against domain-matched medical pretraining. Natural-image SSL may well win, but it is untested here, which makes this a cheap and uncrowded axis once a harness exists.

NOTE: no internet in kernels - a backbone must be a MOUNTED Kaggle model, never a download.

title: Graded targets + confidence as sample weights
description:
Reports are graded, annotations are thresholded: "small joint effusion" can sit against a NEGATIVE annotation because the annotator marked only significant ones. So "term present => positive" is wrong by construction; grade the mention (trace / unqualified / marked) instead - and it costs nothing, because the metric reads only order.

Carry a per-finding confidence as a sample weight so a report that never mentions synovitis pulls weakly on that head rather than asserting a negative. Weight the image-annotated studies above every derived row - they are the only labels read from the images.
close_reason: Both halves shipped: targets.py carries graded scores (docstring 'Graded, not thresholded') and per-(study,target) confidence as loss weights, with annotated studies at W=3.0. The floor on top is knee-9sy, measured and closed.

title: Attention-MIL degenerate attention is a named failure mode with published fixes
description:
ANSWERED by measurement 2026-08-11, and the answer is that the literature does NOT transfer.

The pre-registered test was: 'if withholding any single slot barely moves the number, the collapse is real AND harmless, and the literature does not apply.' Occlusion on base+ranking, 400 holdout studies:
  AX_FLUID_FS   +0.0193   <- the only slot outside the 0.006 noise floor
  COR_FLUID_FS  +0.0094
  SAG_T1        +0.0067
  SAG_FLUID_FS  +0.0056
  COR_T1        +0.0053
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS +0.0042
  spread 0.0151

READ IT HONESTLY, both ways. The collapse is REAL - axial carries 2-4x any other slot, matching the +0.127 attention/anatomy correlation measured earlier. But five of six slots cost less than the noise floor to remove, so the model is not catastrophically single-instance either; it is one dominant slot plus five marginal ones. Withholding the dominant slot costs 0.0193, which is larger than any single method change measured in this project - so the collapse is not FREE either.

WHY THE PATHOLOGY FIXES STILL DO NOT APPLY: ASMIL and AttriMIL treat bags of thousands of instances where attention collapse discards almost all evidence. We have SIX. A stabiliser that spreads attention over six slots is spreading it over slots that measurably carry less, which is not obviously an improvement - and the anatomical prior, which forced exactly that, already measured neutral (0.8073 vs 0.8081).

DOWNGRADING to P3 rather than closing: the papers are still unread, and the one thing that would change this reading is if a stabiliser helps for a reason other than anatomy-correctness. Not worth GPU while knee-am4 (border) and knee-ghd (depth) are open - both are larger effects on the same model.

title: bd dolt auto-push fails on every write: the git remote has no dolt refs
description:
Every bd write prints: 'dolt auto-push failed: push to origin/main: Error 1105 ... git ref not found: refs/dolt/remotes/origin/dolt/data/<uuid>'. beads runs in EMBEDDED mode here (no Dolt server), so 'bd dolt show' is unsupported and .beads is not a dolt repo directory.

IMPACT IS COSMETIC-BUT-NOISY, not data loss: .beads/issues.jsonl is git-tracked and committed, which CLAUDE.md already names as the durable record ('the Dolt engine is gitignored'). Issues are safe. But the session-completion protocol calls 'bd dolt push', and that step can never succeed as configured.

TWO OPTIONS, NOT TAKEN because they change the owner's issue-tracker sync strategy:
  (a) disable the dolt auto-push and rely on the git-tracked jsonl, then drop 'bd dolt push' from the protocol;
  (b) initialise the dolt refs on the remote so the push has somewhere to land.

Owner's call - flagging rather than changing it.

title: archmap costs one extra commit+push cycle - by design, and the CRLF premise was wrong
description:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-08-11, after hitting this twice in ten minutes and actually reading the hook.

WHAT I ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: graph.json re-dirties after every commit with NO content diff, purely from archmap writing CRLF against an LF blob, leaving a permanently dirty tree.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING: .gitattributes already carries '* text=auto eol=lf', so the normalisation is handled - after a commit+push cycle 'git status' comes back CLEAN, verified twice today. The CRLF line in the output is git's normal normalisation notice, not a defect.

The friction that remains is REAL but INTENTIONAL. The archmap hook is pre-push, not pre-commit, and .pre-commit-config.yaml:151-155 states why: commits stay fast, the graph refreshes once before the push that deploys, and if it drifted the hook stages the regen and BLOCKS - 'commit it and push again (the diff stays your reviewable architecture-erosion signal; auto-committing in a hook can't join the in-flight push)'.

So a push that changed any module costs one extra commit+push. That is the price of the architecture-erosion record being a reviewable diff, and it is only paid when the architecture ACTUALLY changed - not every push.

DOWNGRADED P2 -> P3 and left open only as documentation. Do NOT 'fix' this by moving the hook to pre-commit or auto-committing in the hook: the first slows every commit for a signal needed once per push, and the second is what the comment explicitly rules out. Template-owned in any case - it would belong upstream in sdlc-scaffold, not here.
